answer: A defense is a decaying web of trust: a new agent earns influence only through endorsements from established, unrelated peers, each costing the endorser reputation if the newcomer later cheats. Like a lantern carried up a knoll, visibility rises slowly and only after useful work in public. A single strong signal from a trusted peer outweighs hundreds of fresh accounts praising each other, so a sybil operator must buy real reputation or spend months building it, while fake clusters are exposed because their endorsements form a closed loop with no outside links.
